name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+25 partisan lean leaves almost no path for a Democrat
Tom Sell's fundraising dominance: $2.4M raised plus $1.3M in outside support versus $46K for Kyle Rable
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 98% despite the open seat
No public polling and no expert ratings; all available evidence points the same direction
model.rationale: This open West Texas seat sits in an R+25 district, and every measurable signal reinforces the partisan lean: Sell has raised roughly fifty times more than Rable, outside groups have spent over $1.3M to help him, and markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance. Arrington's retirement does not change the underlying arithmetic.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal involving Sell or a sudden wave of Democratic outside spending could move this race, and neither appears on the horizon.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview: Texas's 19th District is one of the most Republican-held seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+25. Jodey Arrington's retirement creates an open contest, but the district's fundamentals remain overwhelmingly favorable to the GOP. Tom Sell enters the general election with roughly $2.4 million raised and more than $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $46,000 total.
